questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place that felt different, but still homey - somewhere I could see myself living.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, but I do not think it would have been that easy if I didn't receive the information on where to look for it by other people. I would not necessarily have figured it out by myself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, I think.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I only applied one place and that was the one I got, so that was pretty smooth.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In my case, I would probably have tried to find something closer to campus. It was only 3 km (50 minute walk and 25 minutes by metro) but there was a lot of commuting forth and back since I that to spend a lot of time on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I thought it was a little tricky to navigate - but I don't know what would have made it easier

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I remember calling in with questions a few times and the response was always useful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had a LOT of problems with getting my schedule to fit - and ended up not getting two of my classes approved by my home university because of their level, and by then it was too late to change them - so that was a real bummer.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to do your research in time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I feel like the level was fitting, but the work load was crazy. I learned a lot, but too much time were spend on "silly" assignments that just stressed me out

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My classes were all really different, so I can not really sum it up. Some were amazing, some were not. But overall I would prefer UCPH - they treat you like an adult.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender & International relations (poli sci)
Gender & sexuality in modern china (his)
Black women in north america (his) 
Indigenous studies of Anthropology (anth)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My course on sexuality and gender in China were probably the most enjoyable course I've ever done. I really loved it.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I spend I lot of money on my phone deal because I forgot to cancel it, but that was just my fault
And I also had to pay 1300 DKK for overweight on the way home...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some random food items were really expensive. 80 DKK for a burrata is insane.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Many more than I had time and energy to do. I went on some outdoor trips and skiing as well. But those were organized by students and you could really tell (not in the best way), but overall it was fun.
I was happy with my gym membership - really nice and cheap.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just do as much as you can - if you have time. I wish I had more time to do more non-academic activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing!! Go to value village and spend all your money. Go for long walks. I walked an average of 16000 steps a day during my exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Hmm, do not go during the winter. People started to open up by April when the weather got nicer.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Canadians are almost too nice (fits the stereotype) and they have a hard time understanding irony.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
That people in general were friendly 
Nice food - good supermarkets as well

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be ready to spend A LOT of time in the library reading and writing - there is a bunch of homework
Be prepared for a looooong winter. I went to the US (New York and then New Orleans) to escape to a warmer climate. It was the best thing I did. Best part of my trip actually. But plan some trips out of town if you have the money.
Try not to let the workload consume you. Make time to be a person, and not just a student.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Probably.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Trying to live in a new place and creating my own routine and enjoying life there
Also all the people I met!
It was all so rewarding despite some tough times (winter time and academia)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The amount of work and assignments - I'm not used to that.
And the problems with getting my courses approved (I'm alright now but it was SO frustrating)
I also got my wallet stolen and lived on borrowed cash for ten days...... So bring an extra credit card!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
